root_cause.text: In `fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c`, `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()` mishandled `nfsd_file` ownership by overwriting `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` without dropping any preexisting reference and by storing the same single reference in both `fi_fds[O_RDONLY]` and `fi_rdeleg_file`, so delegation cleanup could fail to release the file when another read open still kept the access count elevated.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `put_deleg_file()` to call `nfsd_file_put(rnf)` before `nfs4_file_put_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ)`, and changes `nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg()` to only assign `fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] = nf` when that slot is empty, then set `fp->fi_rdeleg_file = nfsd_file_get(fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY])`, and finally `nfsd_file_put(nf)` if the new file wasn’t stored—confirming the bug was a reference leak caused by incorrect reference management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `put_deleg_file()` to release the `rnf` file reference before dropping read access, preventing a reference leak.
intent_record.what: The function `put_deleg_file(struct nfs4_file *fp)` was changed so that the `rnf` pointer is now handled inside a block: when `rnf` is non-NULL, it now calls `nfsd_file_put(rnf)` and then `nfs4_file_put_access(fp, NFS4_SHARE_ACCESS_READ)`. Previously, only `nfs4_file_put_access(...)` was called under the `if (rnf)` condition.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this ensures the referenced `rnf` file object is actually released when present, instead of only dropping the associated read access reference. This prevents a resource leak or mismatched reference accounting for delegated read files.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix delegation file reference handling by only installing nf when needed and using proper get/put semantics for fi_rdeleg_file and nf.
intent_record.what: Inside nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg(), the code no longer unconditionally assigns nf to fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] and fp->fi_rdeleg_file. Instead, after taking fi_lock and incrementing read access, it now checks whether fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is already unset before storing nf there, clears nf to NULL when it is stored, sets fi_rdeleg_file from nfsd_file_get(fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY]), then after unlocking calls nfsd_file_put(nf) if nf was not consumed.
intent_record.how: This changes ownership and reference handling for the file descriptor associated with the delegation. It prevents overwriting an existing O_RDONLY file entry, ensures fi_rdeleg_file always gets a referenced file object derived from the current O_RDONLY slot, and avoids leaking the passed-in nf by dropping its reference only when it was not installed into the file state.
